newsitem.title: BULGARIA: RUSSIA, BULGARIA, GREECE TO MULL OIL ROUTE NOVEMBER.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA, BULGARIA, GREECE TO MULL OIL ROUTE NOVEMBER.

text.p: Russia, Bulgaria and Greece will hold a tripartite meeting in November to discuss the construction of a planned oil route supplying Russian crude to the Balkans, Russia's parliament deputy chairman said.
Mikhail Yuriev told reporters after talks with Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov that Sofia was ready with its feasibility studies, local financial daily Pari reported on Tuesday.
A tripartite meeting at government level has been delayed due to the elections in Russia and Greece, officials said. Bulgaria also has a presidential election on October 27.
Bulgaria's deputy prime minister Doncho Konakchiev said last week the route was now being considered as a part of a greater regional project linking the Black Sea to a Caspian Sea oil pipeline.

Russia, Bulgaria and Greece plan a tanker route from Russia's Novorossiisk to Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Bourgas from where a new high-pressure pipeline would carry Russian crude oil to Alexandroupolis in Greece.
